title: Update on my 3D space exploration game rendered in ASCII
author: Afraid-Act424
selftext:
Hello, following up on [my post](https://www.reddit.com/r/aigamedev/comments/1tu325t/started_a_space_exploration_game_rendered_in/) from last week, here's an update on my exploratory progress.

Quick recap for those who missed it: Spascii is a 3D space exploration game running entirely in the browser, built with three.js, with the whole scene rendered as ASCII characters.

For now I'm still experimenting with mechanics that will help me build the game's universe, along with a few gameplay mechanics.

On the voice side, I switched to Piper, less natural-sounding, but the model I'm using comes with 1000 different voice embeddings, which will let me give a distinct identity to every NPC you interact with.

For data persistence I set up PGlite (combined with Drizzle), a Postgres database that lives directly in the browser (WASM). It opens up a lot of possibilities, especially with support for various extensions like pgvector.

I then dug quite a bit into procedural music generation. Among other things I stumbled upon [https://github.com/vitling/acid-banger](https://github.com/vitling/acid-banger) which gave me plenty of leads to follow. The idea is to have ambient moods in certain zones, but also music that adapts to what you're currently doing. The system is far from perfect for now. It still needs a lot of tuning but the foundations are in place.

My next developments will focus on actual gameplay loops and on NPC interactions. For instance, I'd like interactions to happen directly through voice or through natural-language text, but I don't want to use an LLM to process what the user sends. That would require either heavy resources on the user's machine or going through the cloud. So I have other approaches in mind involving small embedding models, but I'll tell you more about that another time.

You can try out my latest progress at [https://spascii.github.io](https://spascii.github.io)

comments.author: Trashy_io
comments.body: The ASCII style looks really good in the 3d space simulation setting! Really cool project!!

comments.author: DaedalusRaistlin
comments.body:
Dang that looks cool! I was thinking of trying something like this recently, but with a Quake style 3D shooter. Works really well how you've done it. 

My own browser based space sandbox is taking a while. Need something smaller to work on to keep me motivated. Maybe I should give that ascii shooter a proper try. Mainly for the fun of it.

replies.author: Afraid-Act424
replies.body: Thanks, I see what you mean about your space sandbox, it's a never-ending project \^\^ A shooter with that style would look awesome 😄

comments.author: InsensitiveClown
comments.body:
Pretty cool. Now, this may sound crazy, but, can you add old vintage CRT like effects? I mean scanline, refresh band, VHF noise, distortion, vignetting, bloom?
See this: https://analogtv.net/

It would be really cool, giving a kind of Alien (1979) vibe.

replies.author: Afraid-Act424
replies.body: Thanks! Yeah, those kinds of effects would be cool!

comments.author: JD_2020
comments.body:
Hey, just wanted to share this, full disclosure I make this platform WeGPT — but one of the features we put a lot of effort into is no-code agentic playgrounds. I gave this Reddit post to the agent, and prompted it to recreate your game in an interactive playground, and it did a damn good job for one-shot haha.

Here’s the transcript of the chat, you can see my prompt and the steps it took and then the playground link in the final agent response if you want to try out the port of your game.

I’d normally give it some feedback and bug fixes next and have it iterate. It isn’t perfect: https://wegpt.ai/rooms/a001b977-7b22-489a-b033-190eca1cdbe1

replies.author: Afraid-Act424
replies.body: To be honest, that part isn't the most complex. Claude Code built it without any errors in just a few iterations.

replies.body: Yeah, I’m not claiming to have invented fire here. But as an indie dev, bootstrapped startup, I’m pretty satisfied we outperformed Claude code haha
